I am SmallLM, a compact local query-response assistant trained from the data in this repository.
I am an educational assistant that combines instruction retrieval with a character-level text generator.

prompts: what are you able to do
responses: I can answer queries covered by my training data, explain common programming and science concepts, help with writing and planning, perform basic arithmetic, and generate experimental text.
I work best on the topics represented in data/instructions.json. I can also calculate arithmetic and run an interactive chat.
I am a small educational model, not a general-purpose pretrained LLM. I only answer covered topics reliably, I do not browse the web, and important facts should be verified.
My knowledge comes from a small local dataset. I can miss unusual wording and cannot reason broadly like a billion-parameter LLM.

prompts: where do your answers come from
responses: I convert the query into weighted word features, compare it with trained prompt examples, and return a response from the best matching topic when confidence is high enough.
My query mode uses TF-IDF retrieval over instruction examples. Unknown queries receive an honest fallback instead of a fabricated answer.

prompts: how do I train the model
how do I rebuild the trained file
responses: Run: python main.py train. By default it reads data/training.txt and data/instructions.json, then writes model.json.
Add or edit examples in data/instructions.json, then run python main.py train to rebuild the saved model.

prompts: how can I improve this model
responses: Add several realistic prompt paraphrases and concise verified responses for each new topic, retrain, then evaluate with held-out questions that are not exact copies of training prompts.
Improve it by expanding clean instruction data, increasing the from-scratch transformer's capacity, training for more tokens, measuring retrieval accuracy, and evaluating on held-out scenarios.
Temperature changes randomness in character generation. Lower values favor common characters; higher values increase variety. Temperature does not affect the query-response retriever.
Use a lower temperature for predictable continuation and a higher temperature for more surprising text. A value of zero is deterministic.
A random seed initializes the sampler. Reusing the same model, prompt, settings, and seed produces the same sampled output.
Seeds make random experiments reproducible. Change the seed when you want a different sampled result.

prompts: how does a language model work
responses: A language model estimates patterns in sequences of text. Generative models use those patterns to predict or sample what comes next.
A language model learns statistical relationships in text. Large neural models learn many layers of representations; this project demonstrates smaller retrieval and n-gram methods.
An n-gram is a sequence of n items. This model counts which characters follow recent character contexts and backs off to shorter contexts when an exact one is unknown.
Character n-grams model local spelling and phrase patterns. They are simple and fast, but they do not understand long-range meaning.
TF-IDF gives more weight to informative words and less weight to common ones. Cosine similarity then measures how closely a query vector matches each trained prompt vector.
A retrieval assistant selects a stored response associated with the closest training examples. It is grounded and efficient but cannot synthesize arbitrary new knowledge.
A transformer is a neural architecture that uses attention to relate tokens across a sequence. Modern LLMs stack many transformer layers and train on very large datasets.
Attention lets a transformer weigh relevant parts of its input while building contextual representations. This project does not implement a full transformer.

prompts: how do machines learn from data
responses: Machine learning builds systems that learn patterns from examples instead of relying only on hand-written rules.
In machine learning, an algorithm adjusts a model using data so the model can make predictions or decisions on new inputs.
Artificial intelligence is the broad field of building systems that perform tasks associated with perception, reasoning, language, planning, or decision-making.
Machine learning is one approach within artificial intelligence. AI also includes search, planning, knowledge representation, and rule-based methods.

prompts: why does a model memorize training data
how can a model fit noise
responses: Overfitting happens when a model learns training examples too specifically and performs poorly on new data. Use held-out evaluation, more representative data, regularization, or a simpler model to reduce it.
A model that memorizes noise instead of general patterns is overfitting. Always evaluate with examples that were not used during training.
Good training data is relevant, accurate, diverse, consistently formatted, legally usable, and representative of real inputs. Remove duplicates, private information, and incorrect examples.
Data quality sets the ceiling for a small model. Prefer verified examples and realistic paraphrases over large amounts of noisy text.
Python is a general-purpose programming language known for readable syntax and a broad ecosystem. It is widely used for automation, web development, data work, and machine learning.
Python is beginner-friendly while still being useful for production software. This project uses only its standard library.

prompts: how do I define a Python function
responses: Use def, a name, parameters, and an indented body. Example: def add(a, b): return a + b
A Python function is declared with def. Keep it focused, give it a descriptive name, and return a value when the caller needs a result.

prompts: how do I loop in Python
iterate through an array with Python
responses: A for loop iterates over items: for item in items: print(item). Use a while loop when repetition should continue while a condition remains true.
Python for loops work directly with iterables such as lists, ranges, and files. Avoid changing a list while iterating over it unless the behavior is deliberate.

prompts: make a list of squares in Python
compact Python loop for a list
responses: A list comprehension builds a list from an iterable. Example: squares = [number * number for number in range(10)].
Use list comprehensions for short, readable transformations. Prefer a normal loop when the logic has several conditions or side effects.

prompts: what is a good debugging process
my Python code throws an exception
responses: Reproduce the failure, read the complete error, reduce it to the smallest case, inspect assumptions and inputs, change one thing at a time, and add a regression test after fixing it.
Start with evidence: exact inputs, output, stack trace, environment, and the last known working state. A minimal reproducible example makes most bugs easier to isolate.

prompts: how do I design an algorithm
responses: An algorithm is a finite sequence of steps for solving a problem. A good design clearly defines inputs, outputs, edge cases, correctness, and resource costs.
Design an algorithm by stating the problem precisely, considering examples and edge cases, choosing data structures, writing steps, and testing the result.

prompts: what is a variable in programming
responses: A variable is a name associated with a value. Assignment binds or updates that name, and the program can use the value later.
Variables help programs store and refer to state. Their exact typing and lifetime rules depend on the programming language.
Git is a distributed version-control system. It records project history, supports branches, and helps people review and combine changes safely.
Version control lets you inspect changes, restore earlier versions, collaborate, and keep work organized in intentional commits.

prompts: how do I make a git commit
responses: Review git status and the diff, stage only intended files with git add, then run git commit -m followed by a concise message. Push when you are ready to publish.
A good commit contains one coherent change and a message that explains its purpose. Inspect staged changes before committing.

prompts: how is data stored in JSON
what does a JSON object look like
responses: JSON is a text format for objects, arrays, strings, numbers, booleans, and null. Objects use quoted keys, such as {"name": "Mira"}.
JSON is portable and human-readable, but it does not support comments. Validate external JSON before trusting its structure.
An API is a defined way for software components to communicate. It specifies available operations, inputs, outputs, and errors.
Web APIs commonly exchange JSON over HTTP. Good clients handle authentication, timeouts, rate limits, validation, and error responses.

prompts: how does the web transfer data
responses: HTTP is the request-response protocol used by the web. GET usually retrieves a resource, while POST submits data or asks a server to perform an operation.
An HTTP response includes a status code, headers, and often a body. Codes in the 200s generally indicate success, 400s client errors, and 500s server errors.

prompts: how do I build a web page
explain web page structure and style
responses: HTML describes a page's structure and meaning; CSS controls presentation such as layout, color, and spacing. JavaScript can add behavior.
Start a web page with semantic HTML, then use CSS for responsive layout and visual design. Test keyboard access and readable contrast.
SQL is a language for working with relational databases. A basic query is SELECT name FROM users WHERE active = 1;
Relational databases store structured data in tables connected by keys. Parameterize queries instead of concatenating untrusted input.

prompts: how do I stay secure online
responses: Use unique passwords with a password manager, enable multi-factor authentication, install updates, back up important data, and treat unexpected links or attachments cautiously.
Security is risk management. Reduce exposure, use least privilege, keep recoverable backups, and verify important requests through a separate trusted channel.

prompts: how do I create a strong password
responses: Use a password manager to generate and store a unique long password for every account. Enable multi-factor authentication where available.
Do not reuse passwords. A breach at one service can otherwise expose other accounts that share the same credentials.

prompts: how do I spot a phishing email
responses: Phishing uses deceptive messages to steal information or trigger harmful actions. Check the sender and domain, distrust urgency, avoid unexpected attachments, and verify requests through an independent channel.
Do not enter credentials through a link in an unexpected message. Open the known official site yourself and contact the organization directly if unsure.

prompts: how does a plant turn light into energy
how do plants turn light into energy
responses: Photosynthesis is the process by which plants, algae, and some bacteria use light energy to convert carbon dioxide and water into sugars, releasing oxygen as a byproduct.
Plants capture light energy and store it in chemical bonds. The sugars produced support growth and metabolism.

prompts: what is the force pulling us down
responses: Gravity is the attraction between objects with mass. Near Earth it accelerates unsupported objects toward the planet's center.
In general relativity, gravity is described as the curvature of spacetime caused by mass and energy.

prompts: how does water move through nature
responses: The water cycle moves water through evaporation, transpiration, condensation, precipitation, infiltration, and runoff. Solar energy and gravity drive the cycle.
Water evaporates, condenses into clouds, returns as precipitation, and collects in soil, rivers, lakes, oceans, and living things.
DNA is a molecule that stores hereditary information using sequences of four chemical bases. Cells use parts of that information to build functional products such as proteins.
A gene is a region of DNA associated with a functional product. Gene activity is also influenced by regulation and environment.
Weather describes short-term atmospheric conditions at a place and time. Climate describes long-term patterns and distributions of weather over decades or longer.
A cold day is weather; a region's typical seasonal conditions are climate. Individual events do not by themselves establish a climate trend.

prompts: how many planets orbit the sun
responses: The Solar System contains the Sun, eight planets, dwarf planets, moons, asteroids, comets, and smaller bodies. The planets are Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune.
Gravity binds the Solar System. The planets orbit the Sun, while many moons orbit planets and dwarf planets.

prompts: what are protons neutrons and electrons
responses: An atom is the basic unit of a chemical element. It has a nucleus containing protons and usually neutrons, surrounded by electrons described by quantum states.
The number of protons identifies an element. Electron arrangements strongly influence how atoms bond and react.
Electric current is the flow of electric charge. Voltage is electric potential difference, and resistance opposes current.
A closed circuit provides a path for charge flow. Ohm's law relates voltage, current, and resistance for ohmic components: V = I times R.

prompts: what is the capital of France
which city is the French capital
responses: The capital of France is Paris.
In the common seven-continent model they are Africa, Antarctica, Asia, Europe, North America, South America, and Australia. Some regions use different grouping conventions.
The Pacific Ocean is Earth's largest and deepest ocean basin.

prompts: how do I calculate an average
responses: For the arithmetic mean, add all values and divide by the number of values. For example, the mean of 2, 4, and 9 is 15 divided by 3, which is 5.
The word average can mean mean, median, or mode, so identify which measure the situation requires.

prompts: how do I calculate a percentage
what percent is one number of another
responses: To find what percent A is of B, calculate A divided by B times 100, provided B is not zero.
Percent change is (new minus old) divided by the absolute value of old, times 100. State how you handle an old value of zero.

prompts: how do I test if a number is prime
responses: A prime number is an integer greater than one with exactly two positive divisors: one and itself.
To test a positive integer n for primality, check possible factors only through the square root of n. Two is the only even prime.

prompts: how do I break down a task
where should I start on a big task
help me prioritize a large workload
responses: Define the desired outcome and constraints, split the work into testable milestones, identify dependencies and risks, start with the smallest useful deliverable, and review progress at clear checkpoints.
Write down what done means, list the major components, order them by dependency, estimate effort, and choose one concrete next action.

prompts: how can I manage my time
responses: Choose a small number of high-impact priorities, schedule focused blocks, reduce notifications, leave buffer time, and review unfinished work at the end of the day.
Separate urgent work from important work. Limit work in progress and make the next action for each active task specific.

prompts: how can I memorize my class notes
responses: Use active recall, spaced repetition, practice problems, and short explanations in your own words. Test yourself over multiple sessions instead of rereading once.
Set a specific learning goal, study in focused sessions, retrieve ideas from memory, check errors, and revisit difficult material after increasing intervals.
Identify the main claim, essential supporting points, and conclusion. Rewrite them concisely in your own words without adding unsupported ideas.
A good summary preserves the source's meaning and emphasis while removing repetition, minor examples, and unnecessary detail.

prompts: how do I write a professional email
responses: Use a specific subject, a brief greeting, the purpose in the first sentence, necessary context, a clear request or next step, and a polite closing. Proofread names, dates, and attachments.
Keep professional email concise and easy to act on. Put the requested action and deadline in clear language.

prompts: how do I think of more ideas
give me options for a new product
responses: Define the goal and constraints, generate options without judging them, deliberately vary audience, scale, cost, and format, then group and evaluate the strongest ideas.
Try producing ten rough ideas quickly, combining unrelated concepts, reversing assumptions, and asking what the simplest or most ambitious version would be.

prompts: how can I improve my writing
responses: Lead with the main point, prefer concrete nouns and active verbs, remove repetition, vary sentence rhythm, and read the draft aloud. Revise for structure before polishing individual words.
Clear writing gives each paragraph one job. Use examples where they add understanding and delete detail that does not support the purpose.

prompts: how do I teach a complex idea
responses: Start with the purpose, connect the new idea to something familiar, introduce one concept at a time, use a concrete example, and check understanding before adding detail.
A beginner-friendly explanation defines necessary terms, avoids unexplained jargon, and shows one small worked example.
Shrink the task until the first step takes five minutes, remove one distraction, and begin before waiting to feel motivated. Momentum often follows action.
Choose one visible next action and set a short timer. Finishing a small piece is more useful than designing a perfect plan you never start.

prompts: how do I build healthy habits
responses: Start with a small behavior tied to an existing routine, make the environment support it, track consistency without demanding perfection, and adjust gradually. Seek qualified medical advice for health concerns.
Sustainable routines usually include regular sleep, movement, nutritious food, social connection, and recovery, adapted to individual needs and professional guidance.

prompts: help me start a short story
responses: Story prompt: A town's clocks begin counting down to different moments, and the only clockmaker who might understand them has disappeared.
Story prompt: Every night a librarian finds one new book describing the following day, until a blank volume appears with the reader's name on its cover.
Why did the function return early? It had a pressing argument.
A bug walked into a code review. It did not leave, but it did receive several helpful comments.

prompts: you do not know the answer
responses: An unknown result means the query did not match the trained examples strongly enough. Rephrase it using specific topic words or add new verified examples and retrain.
The confidence threshold prevents weak matches from returning unrelated answers. You can expand the dataset rather than lowering the threshold too far.
